column.text: Crypto is in a confirmed risk-off capitulation, with BTC down nearly 6% and more than $1 billion in liquidations flushing out leveraged longs. Long skew is the tell: the long-short ratio sits above 2.9, so the crowd is still leaning the wrong way into a tape that keeps breaking down. Macro is doing the damage. The Nasdaq 100 plunged 6.4% on 5 November, the VIX spiked 70%, SPX fell 4.4%, and NVDA dropped 9%. Dollar liquidity is contracting, and Capital Economics doubts US stocks return to October highs in the short term. Flows confirm the caution. BTC ETFs took in $74.6M on Wednesday 4 Nov, but the seven-day net is still negative at −$752.5M. ETH added $53.0M on Wednesday 4 Nov against a seven-day net of −$515.1M. SOL printed −$1.2M on Thursday 5 Nov, with a seven-day net of −$45.3M. Dip buyers are thin. Whale taker data shows ETH accumulation (+$11M) and BTC distribution (−$1.8M), and a 1h RSI near 31 sets up a squeeze. Oversold alone doesn't qualify as a long, though. Fear & Greed at 28 signals fear, not a bottom. Desk stance: favor continuation shorts and treat failed rallies as better-odds shorts. A long needs a real mechanism, such as deeply negative funding, a clear capitulation reading, a demand catalyst, or a failed breakdown. Until dollar liquidity turns, every bounce is a short until proven otherwise.
